title: The Fakir and His Jar of Butter
summary: An impoverished holy man in a village in India received as an alms a large earthenware jar filled with pure clarified butter. He carried it home, tied it securely with a stout h...
keywords: the fakir and his jar of butter
full_text:
An impoverished holy man in a village in India received as an alms a large earthenware jar filled with pure clarified butter. He carried it home, tied it securely with a stout hemp cord, and suspended it from the ceiling beam directly above the head of his sleeping mat.

Lying on his back with his wooden staff in his hand, staring up at the jar, he began to build magnificent castles in the air:

'When the price of butter rises this winter, I shall sell this jar for ten silver rupees. With those ten rupees, I shall buy five female goats. The goats will give birth to kids every six months, and within five years I shall possess a herd of three hundred goats!

Then I shall sell the goats and buy a hundred cows and two bullocks. I shall buy fertile fields of rice and sugarcane, build a magnificent white mansion with four verandas, and marry the daughter of the wealthiest merchant in the district!

We will have a son as radiant as the moon. When he grows into youth, if he disobeys my commands or neglects his studies in grammar, I shall take my wooden staff and beat him thus, to teach him obedience!'

Lost in his grandiose delusion, the fakir swung his heavy wooden staff with all his might into the air!

The staff struck the suspended earthenware jar squarely in the center. The jar shattered into fifty pieces, and the entire gallon of greasy, yellow butter poured down directly onto his face, beard, and chest, soaking his blankets and covering him in greasy slime!

He sat up spluttering, weeping over his ruined treasure, while the neighbors laughed at how he had destroyed his real butter in pursuit of a phantom son.
moral: Daydreaming of haughty triumph without laying the foundation of honest labor shatters reality into dust.
